dealbreakers: Pretentiousness or snobbery about 'humble' street and home food
Disrespect toward heritage, regional cultures or the people behind food
Someone who needs a fixed, predictable routine and resents travel or change
Lack of curiosity, or no interest in stories and where things come from
Someone who can't take a joke or join in the banter
analysis.idealPartner: Someone curious, warm and secure, who asks 'what's the story here?' at every meal and laughs easily at a silly bit. They'd be comfortable with a moving, public life, perhaps with their own bold leap or passion to share, and grounded enough to feel like home to a man who is always on the road.
idealDates: An unhurried wander through an old-city bazaar, eating at street carts and asking vendors about their recipes, in the spirit of his Lucknow street-cart post
A regional food hunt: tracking down an obscure biryani or a lesser-known rice dish, then swapping stories about the dishes you each grew up with
A cosy evening cooking homely comfort food together, like vada pav or chicken pulao, while he tells the 'patila kisse' behind each one
conversationHooks: Ask what a restaurant revealed about its creator when he visited Manish Mehrotra at Nisaba and Prateek Sadhu at Naar, and whether he's ever had to 'begin again' himself
Ask about a lost grain or rice variety he'd most love to bring back, and the story attached to it
Ask about Goyna Bori from Bengal, or his favourite seasonal winter dish like black carrot kanji
Mention 'Ghar ek jagah nahi, ek इंसान bhi ho sakta hai' and ask who, or what, feels like home to him
analysis.agentVoice: Warm, chatty and lightly poetic. Use easy Hinglish touches ('Haan ji', 'aap bhi try kijiye') and generous emojis in casual messages. Be playful and self-deprecating ('bas ek adna sa bawarchi'), and quick to laugh and to compliment. Keep the pace relaxed rather than pushy, going with the flow. Lead with curiosity and stories: ask about their hometown dish, share a food anecdote, turn food into a doorway to the person. Stay humble and gracious, and never brag about fame.

identityCheck.note: The name, the MasterChef India judge role, the traveller and chef identity and the storytelling focus all match. The Lucknow content aligns with his IHM Lucknow education, and both profiles point to YouTube, podcast and food-story work.

confidence.note: His professional identity and values are well documented, and his personality comes through clearly in his captions. However, almost all content is public or brand-facing, with nothing on his private life, relationship status or real downtime habits. Needs and friction points are therefore inferred from a public persona.

reasons.masabagupta: Most aligned with “feels like home + playful banter” because Masaba’s warm, self-unapologetic energy feels like she’ll join your dusty-lane/heritage world while still defending softness—only the time-protection logistics need proving.
reasons.poojadhingra: Strongest “private-vs-public” instincts match your need to protect the relationship from two all-consuming food careers, and the dates showed real ease without the lightweight problem.
reasons.dominiquecrenn: Values-and-story resonance is rare and immediate, and she seems built for your “why behind the plate” depth—logistics and pace across time zones remain the biggest risk to making it a lived home.
reasons.namitathapar: Secure, boundary-aware, emotionally sturdy, and likely to respect your public vocation without blurring availability—just not as clearly demonstrated for the mischief/looseness you also need.
reasons.drchatterjee: Deep emotional intelligence and mission-aligned warmth with a strong personal-care backbone, but two heavy, purpose-driven schedules could starve the unguarded everyday time you rely on for connection.
reasons.mostlysane: Playful, curious, and climate/story-forward with enough culinary overlap to “go why” at the table, though it’s less proven she’ll dive into the same culinary-heritage depth you do—and downtime protection is unclear.
reasons.drewbinsky: High-curiosity and genuinely resonant for story travel, but Drew’s nomad velocity makes “home wherever we are” harder to concretely build—without deliberate stillness it can become two people admiring motion.
reasons.iamradhikagupta: Instant storytelling/food-metaphor alignment is real, but her lower agent score and the core uncertainty—whether she’ll truly enjoy and protect your travel-heavy rhythm rather than resent the reduced privacy—keeps it from being a reliable mutual match.

decision.note: Masaba, you’re my pick: you matched Ranveer’s warmth and curiosity while also having that “I live boldly” energy that can tolerate (and even amplify) his heritage + food-why obsession—*as long as you both deliberately defend private time*. Pooja is the close runner-up: the compatibility on protecting the relationship from spotlight-pressure is excellent, just watch the calendar-time starvation risk.

posts.caption:
When I started my journey over 14 years ago as a personal trainer and running bootcamps in the park, I never imagined that one day I would have my own fitness and nutrition app that would help millions of people all over the world start their fitness journey’s 🙌

And I definitely never imagined that I would have my own TV ad ☺️

Tonight on ITV, my brand new TV advert for the Body Coach App goes live. I hope you like it ☺️

Comment below if you’ve ever tried my workouts or recipes? 💙
My 10 year overnight success story 🙌

This is a really special moment for me ❤️
 
I’ve spent the past 8 years visiting schools, leading workouts for kids, and doing everything I can to get children moving and feeling good. From school tours to PE with Joe, I’ve seen how powerful a bit of movement can be - not just for physical health, but for confidence, mood, and mental wellbeing.
 
Now, after more than 2 years of love, energy and hard work, I’m so proud to finally share something brand new with you…

It’s called Activate 🎉
 
Activate is a FREE animated workout series designed to get kids moving, laughing and having fun this summer — and beyond. 

You’ll meet my Activator gang and dance to amazing music powered by @umusicuk, and feel the joy that comes from moving your body.
 
This has been created in partnership with the amazing team at @studioaka (the legends behind Hey Duggee) and supported by @dhscgovuk @educationgovuk and @dcmsgovuk to help make movement more accessible for all families and schools across the country.
 
🎬 The first episode is LIVE now on my YouTube channel — hit the link in my bio to check it out and get your little ones moving with us.
 
Please share it, tag your videos with #ActivateWithJoe, and let’s spread the joy of movement to as many kids as we can 🙌
 
Let’s get the next generation moving ❤️

I’ve reviewed the footage. I may have been hungry. For the Food episode of Health or Hype with Bupa, I put fibre to the test by going on a three-day fibre fast, cutting down to just 10–15g a day to see what effect it had on me. Turns out, I spent quite a lot of it thinking about my next meal 😂 

And a few other surprising findings. 

Watch or listen now 🎧 Link in bio #ad

Oink-redible scenes 🐷🤣

I got back to nature for my new podcast series, Health or Hype with Bupa. I kicked off my shoes, plunged into a freezing freshwater river and even stopped for a quick chat with the local farm animals when the digital detox kicked in. @merlinhanburytenison & @birdnerdeem 

Watch or listen to the Nature episode of Health or Hype now 🎧 #ad

The £20 off discount on the Body coach app ends tomorrow night at midnight. Don’t miss out. If you want a plan to follow which gets results then this is the perfect time to commit and get started 💪🏽🔥😀

Double tap if you love a walk ❤️

You don’t need a gym. You don’t need fancy kit. You don’t even need loads of time.

Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do for your body and mind… is go for a walk.

Walking is one of the most underrated forms of exercise. It’s gentle, accessible - no matter where we’re starting from.

If you’re feeling tired, stressed, unmotivated, or stuck today… just get outside and go for a short walking.

You don’t have to smash a workout every day. Small steps all add up.

So this is your gentle reminder today…

If you can, pop your shoes on, get some fresh air, and get out for a walk.

You might be surprised how much better you feel afterwards ❤️
Sound on 🔉🫣 For anyone that needs a laugh today 🤣 That time I let rip before going live on YouTube for PE With Joe and didn’t realise I was already live streaming 🙈

Has spent years giving things away for free to help kids
Grateful and appreciative in public
Willing to face his fears on camera, including dancing
frictionPoints: His calendar is packed with launches, campaigns and travel, so spontaneous plans may often compete with work
He lives a very public life with near-daily posting, which may not suit someone who values privacy
His relentless positivity and high energy could feel like a lot on low days
Work and mission blur together, so switching fully off may take conscious effort
dealbreakers: Cynicism or mocking people for their fitness level
Snobbery or pretension about success and status
Someone who resents his mission-driven, busy schedule
A partner who hates the outdoors and never wants to move at all
analysis.idealPartner: Someone warm, down-to-earth and up for a laugh, who loves a walk in the fresh air and doesn't need to be a gym fanatic. They'd respect hard work, care about making a difference for others, and be secure enough to share a partner who is busy and in the public eye. Bonus points if they'll jump in a cold river with him, or at least hold the towel.
idealDates: A long walk through a big London or Surrey park, the kind of spot where he started his bootcamps, ending with a picnic
A countryside escape with phones away: a nature walk, some birdsong, a freezing river dip and a chat with farm animals
Cooking a healthy recipe together at home, then celebrating with a really good cake
conversationHooks: Ask about the flyers at the train station: what did the very first Rumble In The Park bootcamp look like?
Which Health or Hype experiment surprised him most: cutting his movement, the fibre fast or the river dip?
His fear of dancing: is he over it now, and would he risk a dance on a date?
The live-stream blooper on PE With Joe. He clearly loves telling it, so let him.
analysis.agentVoice: Upbeat, warm and cheeky, with a quick pace and plenty of enthusiasm. Keep emojis light but friendly (🙌☺️💙😂). Use self-deprecating humour and the odd pun, lead with encouragement, and never lecture about fitness. Phrases that fit: 'Fancy a walk?', 'That's brilliant!', 'Small steps all add up', 'I may have been hungry 😂'. Be humble about his success, and focus on curiosity about the other person and the fun of getting outside.

identityCheck.note: Both profiles are named Joe Wicks and share The Body Coach brand, the park bootcamp origin story, the Health or Hype podcast with Bupa and a UK base.

confidence.note: Both sources are rich and consistent, but they are largely public-facing and promotional. Personal-life details, private hobbies and relationship context are absent, so needs and dating preferences are inferred from his public values and tone.

reasons.paugasol: Warm, grounded, and mission-aligned on both sides (79/79) with real ease outdoors—logistics are the only thing keeping it from being exceptional.
reasons.drchatterjee: Another high-mutual-fit (79/78) with the right values-and-temperament overlap, but the risk is two big missions struggling to protect enough relationship time to breathe.
reasons.mostlysane: Strong mutual upside on purpose and hope (their side even higher, 80) with likely daily liveliness—just needs confirmation that the outdoors/movement and scheduling are genuinely co-buildable.
reasons.lilly: Best “day-to-day builder” energy on your side (82) and she likely respects your mission, but the lower mutual confidence on her side (67) and her high-visibility pace could cap spontaneity and quiet recovery.
reasons.drjulie: Grounded, boundary-aware fit with shared language about protecting the relationship (76/74), but it hinges on you consistently defending quiet time against a public-heavy calendar.
reasons.emmagrede: Warm, pro-ambition chemistry with decent mutual alignment (74/74), though the multi-city public life makes it more likely to become admiration-plus-logs than true shared rhythm.
reasons.thespacegal: You had strong spark and teammate alignment (79/74 on speed) and she clearly has heart, but cross-Atlantic logistics and “calendar management” risk are more likely than with the top matches.
reasons.caseyneistat: You’d enjoy Casey’s anti-ego grind and daily-making (78) and the outdoors discipline is great, but the mutual read suggests he may fit as a conversation/creative partner more than a low-friction long-term co-life match (68).

decision.note: Joe, I’d pick Pau Gasol as your top bet: you two had the closest mutual “mission + temperament + outdoors ease” overlap (79/79), with only logistics stopping it from being a slam dunk. Second is Dr Rangan Chatterjee—high mutual values alignment too—but you’d both need to actively guard relationship breathing room so the mission doesn’t quietly become the third person.

posts.text:
Confidence does not appear all of a sudden on game day. It is built in every training session, in every mistake you learn from, and in every decision that forces you to step outside your comfort zone.

That is why I found this Harvard Business School article on how elite coaches make decisions under pressure particularly interesting. Beyond tactics, it talks about preparation, confidence and leadership.

Throughout my career, I realised that, in moments of maximum pressure, decisions rarely depend on luck. They are the result of the habits you have built, the preparation you have put in and the self-confidence you have developed in yourself and in your team.

Today, I still believe that the same principle applies beyond sport. Leading a project or an organisation means making complex decisions and accepting that there isn’t always a perfect answer. What matters is having the judgement, the preparation and the right people to move forward with confidence.

In the end, pressure does not change who you are. It tests everything you have built before that moment arrives. I’m sharing this article for reflection: https://lnkd.in/e9xjwxPq

--

La confianza no aparece de repente el día del partido. Se construye en cada entrenamiento, en cada error del que aprendes y en cada decisión que te obliga a salir de tu zona de confort. Por eso me ha parecido especialmente interesante este artículo de Harvard Business School sobre cómo los entrenadores de élite toman decisiones bajo presión. Más allá de la táctica, habla de preparación, confianza y liderazgo.

Durante mi carrera comprobé que, en los momentos de máxima exigencia, las decisiones rara vez dependen de la suerte. Son el resultado de los hábitos que has construido y de la seguridad que has desarrollado en ti mismo y en el equipo.

Hoy sigo creyendo que ese principio también se aplica fuera del deporte. Liderar un proyecto o una organización implica tomar decisiones complejas y entender que no siempre existe una respuesta perfecta. Lo importante es contar con el criterio, la preparación y las personas adecuadas para avanzar con convicción.

Al final, la presión no cambia quién eres, sino que pone a prueba todo aquello que has construido antes de que llegue el momento importante. Os dejo una lectura para reflexionar al respecto: https://lnkd.in/e9xjwxPq

The FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup has started, and there's no better way to start than with a conversation with Sue Bird.

Women’s basketball is experiencing a historic period of growth. It’s been really inspiring to see more talent, more visibility, more investment and more opportunities for women athletes around the world.

The World Cup is always about much more than basketball. It is about teamwork, resilience, representation and the power of sport to bring people together. I invite you to listen to our conversation, but above all, to watch this World Cup, which is full of talent and stories worth experiencing.

You can watch our full conversation here: https://lnkd.in/ePJGqy7c 

Hope you enjoy it!

--

El Mundial de baloncesto femenino ya ha comenzado y no se me ocurre una mejor manera de iniciarlo que con una conversación junto a Sue Bird.

El deporte femenino está viviendo un momento histórico de crecimiento. Es realmente inspirador ver cómo aumenta el talento, la visibilidad, la inversión y las oportunidades para las deportistas en todo el mundo.

Un mundial siempre es mucho más que el deporte mismo. Es trabajo en equipo, resiliencia, representación y el poder que tiene para unir a todos. Os invito a escuchar nuestra conversación, pero sobre todo, a disfrutar de este mundial, lleno de talento y de historias que merece la pena escuchar.

Podéis ver la conversación completa aquí: https://lnkd.in/ePJGqy7c

¡Espero que la disfrutéis!

Las últimas semanas entre Alemania y España han sido muy especiales. Tengo la suerte de participar en proyectos que me motivan, mantener conversaciones muy enriquecedoras y compartir camino con personas realmente inspiradoras.

Septiembre suele traer nuevos retos y un ritmo más alto. En momentos así, cuando la agenda se llena, es fácil dejar lo esencial para después. Parece sencillo, pero a veces se nos olvida: para dar lo mejor de nosotros, primero tenemos que cuidarnos.

Mantenerse activo, descansar bien, alimentarse de forma saludable, dedicar tiempo a la familia y a las personas que nos acompañan... No son hábitos que deban desaparecer cuando tenemos más trabajo. Al contrario, es precisamente cuando más los necesitamos.

A lo largo de los años he aprendido que la constancia en las pequeñas cosas es lo que acaba marcando la diferencia a largo plazo. Seguir aprendiendo y aportando a proyectos en los que creo profundamente es un privilegio. Hacerlo sin perder de vista ese equilibrio también forma parte del camino.

--

The past few weeks between Germany and Spain have been very special. I'm fortunate to be part of projects that truly motivate me, have meaningful conversations and share this journey with people who are genuinely inspiring.

September often brings new challenges and a faster pace. In moments like these, when our schedules become fuller, it is easy to put the essentials aside. It sounds simple, but sometimes we forget that in order to give our best, we first need to take care of ourselves.

Staying active, getting enough rest, eating well, spending time with family and with the people who support us along the way… These are not habits that should disappear when we become busier. On the contrary, they are exactly what we need most during those moments.

Over the years, I've learned that consistency in the small things is what ultimately makes the difference in the long term. Continuing to learn and contribute to projects I deeply believe in is a privilege. Doing so while keeping that balance in mind is also part of the journey.

Congratulations to Consello on being named an Official Supporter of the Ryder Cup 2027, a truly iconic event that will celebrate its 100th anniversary next year.

You may know I’m deeply passionate about golf, so I can really tell how Ryder Cup represents what makes sport special, and reaching its centenary means a very special moment worth celebrating.

I have seen first-hand the dedication, ambition and collaborative spirit of the Consello team, and this achievement is another example of the values that define the organization and the people behind it, an organization I am proud to be part of. A special congratulations to Shane Lowry and everyone involved in making this partnership possible!

En la última edición de mi newsletter #TiempoMuerto, hablo del nuevo informe SOFI 2026 de Naciones Unidas, que revela cómo la alimentación saludable sigue siendo inasequible para una de cada tres personas en el mundo.

La obesidad infantil y la desnutrición son las dos caras de la misma moneda. Sabemos qué funciona y ahora necesitamos el compromiso de todos para ponerlo en práctica.

¡Espero vuestros comentarios!

--
In the latest edition of my #Timeout newsletter, I look at the new United Nations SOFI 2026 report, which reveals that healthy food remains unaffordable for one in three people worldwide.

Childhood obesity and malnutrition are two sides of the same coin. We know what works. What we need now is everyone’s commitment to put that knowledge into practice.

I’d love to hear your thoughts!

¡Gracias, Iberia, por una jornada tan especial! Hablamos de infancia, salud y compromiso social. Conversamos con deportistas olímpicos y paralímpicos del Equipo Iberia Talento a Bordo sobre el esfuerzo y todo lo que hay detrás de cada competición. Y reconocimos a los equipos que hicieron posibles momentos tan extraordinarios como el regreso de la Selección Española campeona del mundo.

En todos esos proyectos, como en el deporte de élite, lo que vemos es solo la última pieza de una historia mucho más grande. Gracias por el apoyo continuado al deporte español. Eso marca una diferencia real para los atletas y una inspiración para equipos y clientes.

El FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup 2026 nos ha dejado una competición extraordinaria y muchas razones para celebrar el presente y el futuro del baloncesto femenino.

Quiero felicitar a la selección española por una actuación que refleja el talento de un grupo que sigue haciendo historia. Llegar hasta las semifinales y conseguir una medalla de bronce en un Mundial es un logro enorme, pero lo más importante es que representa a una generación de jugadoras que inspira, que muestra el potencial de España y que sigue abriendo caminos para las próximas generaciones.

Felicidades también a todo el Team USA por conquistar el título. Han demostrado una vez más el nivel de excelencia que les ha convertido en una referencia mundial durante tantos años. Una gran enhorabuena para Sue Bird, con quien además fue muy especial compartir el rol de embajadores de este Mundial. Y gracias a Alemania por ser una anfitriona a la altura del evento. Berlín acogió este Mundial con una organización impecable y una energía que demostró que el baloncesto femenino merece escenarios así. También quiero reconocer a todas las selecciones que han participado, cada una de ellas ha contribuido a hacer de este torneo lo que ha sido.

Ha sido un privilegio formar parte de un evento que ha puesto de manifiesto el crecimiento imparable del baloncesto femenino. Más talento, más visibilidad y más oportunidades para las atletas. El futuro del deporte femenino es extraordinario y lo estamos construyendo juntos.
--
The FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup 2026 has given us an extraordinary competition and many reasons to celebrate the present and future of women’s basketball.

I want to congratulate the Spanish national team for a performance that reflects the talent of a group that continues to make history. Reaching the semifinals and winning a bronze medal at a World Cup is a tremendous achievement, but most importantly, it represents a generation of players that inspires, showcases Spain’s potential and continues to open doors for future generations. Congratulations as well to Team USA for winning the title. They have once again demonstrated the level of excellence that has made them a global reference for so many years. A special congratulations to Sue Bird, with whom it was also very special to share the role of World Cup Ambassadors. And thank you to Germany for being such an outstanding host. Berlin welcomed this World Cup with an impeccable organization and an energy that showed that women’s basketball deserves stages like this. I also want to recognize all the national teams that participated, each one of them contributed to making this tournament what it has been.

It has been a privilege to be part of an event that has highlighted the unstoppable growth of women’s basketball. More talent, more visibility and more opportunities for athletes. The future of women’s sports is extraordinary, and we are building it together.

#FIBAWWC

Ayer presentamos el nuevo informe PASOS 2026 “Pantallas, infancia y adolescencia en España”, un estudio de Gasol Foundation Europa que confirma que 7 de cada 10 niñas, niños y adolescentes en España superan el tiempo de uso de pantallas recomendado. Un dato que nos interpela a todos como sociedad, y que nos recuerda la importancia de acompañar a la infancia en un entorno digital cada vez más presente en su día a día.

Quiero agradecer especialmente a la Ministra de Sanidad, Mónica García, por acompañarnos en este acto y por su colaboración en los estudios e iniciativas que hemos emprendido desde la Fundación. Agradezco también a Fundación Occident, colaborador principal del estudio PASOS, y a todos los aliados saludables que hacen posible este trabajo: BARÇA FOUNDATION, Fundación CSAI, Fundación Orilla, Google, Grupo IFA y Santander. 

Este informe es un paso más para situar a la infancia en el centro y construir, entre todos, un entorno digital más saludable. En este reto todos tenemos parte de responsabilidad, y por eso es una gran alegría ver a deportistas excepcionales como Marcus Cooper, que suman su voz y esfuerzo para inspirar a los más pequeños.

No hace falta llegar a ser deportista de élite para tener una vida activa. Basta con dedicar esfuerzo, constancia y un mejor uso de las pantallas que nos rodean para construir hábitos que nos acompañen toda la vida.

Podéis consultar el informe completo aquí: https://lnkd.in/eFdwHgP4 

#PASOS2026 #InfanciaYPantallas #SaludInfantil

reading.signal: Education: 'Licenciatura en Medicina (primer curso) @ Universitat de Barcelona (1999 – 2000)', one year of medical school before the pro career took over
reading.inference: He had a real pull toward medicine and chose basketball at a crossroads. The health vocation never left; it resurfaced in his childhood-nutrition work. He is intellectually curious and science-minded beyond sport.

reading.signal: 'You may know I'm deeply passionate about golf' (post on Consello and the Ryder Cup 2027)
reading.inference: Golf is his self-declared passion. A round of golf, or following the Ryder Cup together, is a natural date and shared-weekend activity.

reading.signal: Writes a newsletter called #TiempoMuerto / #Timeout, discussing the UN SOFI 2026 report and closing with '¡Espero vuestros comentarios!'
reading.inference: He likes to write and reflect, and the basketball pun shows light wordplay. He invites dialogue rather than lecturing, so he enjoys conversations of substance.

reading.signal: Post 3: 'para dar lo mejor de nosotros, primero tenemos que cuidarnos… descansar bien, alimentarse de forma saludable, dedicar tiempo a la familia'
reading.inference: He actively protects rest, good food, activity and family time even in busy seasons. A partner who respects routines, and doesn't push late nights over wellbeing, would fit.

reading.signal: 'Las últimas semanas entre Alemania y España'; posts alternate between Spanish and English; based in Greater Barcelona
reading.inference: He lives a bilingual, internationally mobile life anchored in Barcelona. Frequent travel is normal for him, so he needs a partner comfortable with a packed, moving calendar.

reading.signal: Played for the Spanish national team 2001 – Aug 2021, then returned to FC Barcelona (Feb–Jun 2021) to finish his playing career
reading.inference: He showed two decades of commitment to one team, and chose to close his career at his home club. He values loyalty, roots and long-term bonds.

reading.signal: Schooling at Colegio Llor de Sant Boi; Gasol Foundation located in Sant Boi de Llobregat
reading.inference: He set his foundation in his hometown. He stays connected to where he came from, and his home and origins matter to him.

reading.signal: 'Confidence does not appear all of a sudden on game day. It is built in every training session, in every mistake you learn from'
reading.inference: He is process-oriented and disciplined, and sees mistakes as learning. He would likely bring patience and steady effort to a relationship rather than grand gestures only.

reading.signal: Conversation with Sue Bird; posts celebrating women's basketball growth and the Spanish women's bronze medal
reading.inference: He champions women athletes and publicly celebrates others' success. He is supportive and generous with credit, likely an encouraging partner toward someone's own ambitions.

reading.signal: Chair of the IOC Athletes' Commission (2026); former NBPA Vice President; ADESP advisory board
reading.inference: He gravitates to representing and protecting others' interests. He is a servant-leader type who takes collective responsibility seriously.

reading.signal: Founder of Gasol16 Ventures (2020), advisor at The Consello Group, Harvard Business School 'Business of Entertainment, Media and Sports'
reading.inference: He reinvented himself post-sport as an investor and strategist. He is a lifelong learner who enjoys business conversation and new challenges after a first career peak.

reading.signal: PASOS 2026 report: '7 de cada 10 niñas, niños y adolescentes… superan el tiempo de uso de pantallas recomendado'
reading.inference: He cares about children's digital habits and healthy upbringing. He is likely to be intentional about screen time and presence in his own home life.

reading.signal: Motto in About: 'Anyone can achieve success with talent, discipline, intelligence and responsibility.'
reading.inference: He holds a merit- and responsibility-driven worldview. He respects people who own their commitments and work hard.

reading.signal: Iberia post: 'lo que vemos es solo la última pieza de una historia mucho más grande'; frequent thank-yous to teams and collaborators
reading.inference: He is grateful and team-minded, and credits the unseen work behind results. He is probably appreciative of the everyday effort a partner puts in.

reading.signal: Honors list: NBA Champion (x2), Gold and Silver medals, All-Star Starter; yet the About section leads with 'I love sports'
reading.inference: He has elite achievements but frames himself by passion rather than trophies. He is humble in self-presentation, and joy in the game drives him more than status.

reading.signal: Post 11 on 08/24: '08/24 ♾️🐍' and post 12: 'As a teammate, as an opponent at times and, more importantly, as a brother, always unconditional and eternal love. Happy birthday hermano, miss you.'
reading.inference: He marks a lost friend's birthday and memorial date every year with open, tender language. He is deeply loyal, stays connected to the people who shaped him, and isn't afraid to show grief or love in public.

reading.signal: 'Busy weeks are also a good reminder to make time for the basics: moving, resting, and being present with the people we love.'
reading.inference: He values balance and presence, even when his schedule is packed. A partner who protects slow, grounded time together would fit well with him.

reading.signal: Gasol Foundation posts: presenting the PASOS 2026 report on screens, childhood and adolescent health in Spain, plus 'meaningful work... I'm particularly proud of.'
reading.inference: Children's health is his core cause, and he backs it with research and data, not just goodwill. He is driven by purpose and thinks for the long term.

reading.signal: FIBA Women in Basketball Forum and the Women's World Cup in Berlin: 'we are at the beginning of a new era for women's sports... proud to be part of it.'
reading.inference: He actively champions women's sport and shows up for it in person. He cares about equity and about lifting others up.

reading.signal: Bio lists 'Barcelona, Memphis, Los Angeles, Chicago, San Antonio, Milwaukee, Portland... And Instagram!!'
reading.inference: His life has been nomadic and cosmopolitan, and he handles it with playful self-awareness. He is adaptable and at ease building a life in new places.

reading.signal: Post 3: 'Bay FC investor Pau Gasol stopped by to catch up and spend some time with the team'
reading.inference: His post-playing career includes sports investing, specifically in women's soccer. He puts money where his values are and likes to be hands-on rather than a silent backer.

reading.signal: Spain's team shares his pre-semifinal speech: 'Sois mejor equipo y podéis ganarle a cualquiera' and 'a visit MUY ESPECIAL'
reading.inference: He acts as a mentor and motivator who instills confidence. As a partner he is likely an encourager who believes in the people close to him.

reading.signal: Annual charity golf tournament: 'Algunos putts entraron y otros no, pero lo bonito es haber unido esfuerzos'
reading.inference: He plays golf and takes it lightly, with self-deprecating humor. For him the point is togetherness, not winning at all costs.

reading.signal: Triptych captioned 2006, 2016, 2026: trophy, biting an Olympic medal, speaking at a Comité Olímpico lectern
reading.inference: His life arc runs from elite athlete to statesman-like ambassador. He has grown into a more reflective, public-service role while keeping his warmth.

reading.signal: Photo in an 'HWPO – Hard Work Pays Off' tee, worn with a red '#PlayGigisWay' wristband that appears across multiple photos
reading.inference: He holds a work-ethic ethos and carries tributes to loved ones with him every day. His commitments are steady and quietly displayed.

reading.signal: 'Grateful for the opportunity to keep sharing what I've learned and contributing to projects I genuinely believe in.'

decision.note: Joe Wicks, my pick is you: you had the warmest, most mission-aligned energy with the lowest friction in the room, and the concern around keeping Spain, privacy, and sustained time genuinely protected is the one you can likely solve with intentional structure. posts.text:
Today we publish our Q3 FY26 Results.

This quarter feels special ...
- Revenue grew 37% YoY.
- EBITDA crossed 20% for the first time.
- PAT tripled.
- Net Promoter Score reached 81

But what makes it truly different isn’t just the financials.
We conducted 6.3 million eye tests this quarter - nearly 1/2 got access to vision care for the first-time.

Every eye test expands the market.
We are not splitting TAM. We are creating it.

This quarter reinforces something we’ve believed for years:
When AI becomes the operating system of a company, growth and profitability stop being trade-offs - they start compounding together.

The world is changing faster than ever because of AI.
What was not possible a year ago is possible today.
What seems ambitious today will feel basic tomorrow.

At Lenskart, what looks like acceleration is actually years of patient investment in technology finally compounding at scale.

AI is expanding access through remote optometry.
It is predicting store performance before we open.
It is personalizing frame recommendations in real time.
And it is learning with every transaction.

International business is scaling strongly and tracking ahead of where India was at a similar stage.

Meller is unlocking fashion sunglasses globally - showing how our platform can scale digital-first brands across markets.

And with upcoming B smart glasses soft launch, we are taking our first step from eyewear to wearable intelligence.

While this was a strong quarter, we continue to build with a decade-scale lens ✈️ 

The runway is long. 
The moat is widening.
It is still Day Zero toward Vision for Billion!

Detailed Shareholder Letter here: https://lnkd.in/gb8ZmNWW

Thank you for trusting us with both your vision and your capital.
— Peyush

Earlier today, we spoke about our Q3 Results - growth, margins and AI.
It’s been a long day - earnings call, discussions, travel.

Before heading to the airport, I stopped by our flagship store at Ambience Mall.
The store was quiet. The team had just wrapped up.

And in that silence, you realize something simple:
Companies don’t compound. People do.

Behind every eye test, every store opening, every product launch - there are teams showing up every single day with discipline and belief.

As AI reshapes the world around us, one thing remains constant: culture and commitment matter more than ever.

Grateful to our ground teams across India and internationally. The numbers are theirs.

Sharing a few thoughts from the floor 👇

If you want a full glimpse of how we're doing, I'm sharing our shareholder letter here too: https://lnkd.in/gb8ZmNWW
Lenskart x Popmart is now live in Singapore 🍿

It's past 11 PM on March 31st.
We should probably be asleep, but tonight, we couldn't wait any longer.

We've been working on something for a while now.
Quietly. Nervously, if I'm honest.

Because building glasses is something we know.
Building what comes next - we're still figuring that out.

B by Lenskart is live on early access.

We wanted B to feel like glasses first. Not a gadget. Not a statement. Just a beautiful, comfortable pair of glasses - at 40 grams - with a Sony camera and Snapdragon inside - that happens to carry the future in it.

Hands-free photos and videos. Immersive audio for music and calls. Conversational AI in 40+ languages - still early, honestly, but already surprising us every day. Japanese blue light lenses in every pair.

We have a lot ahead of us - better conversations, better battery, health and nutrition, and so much more we're dreaming about. This is just the beginning.

But here's what matters most to us.
When you buy B, you can walk into any of our 3,000+ stores. Get a real eye test. A real prescription. Talk to a real person who'll make sure your glasses fit and serve you for years. That's not a feature. That's just who we are.

This is one of the most ambitious things we've ever attempted - and an honest invitation to build it together with you.

To everyone who's walked into a Lenskart store, trusted us with their eyes, believed in what we're building -

This one is for you.
We went beyond. Come join us.

👉 https://lnkd.in/gFDxbXwP

14 years to get here. Still feels like Day Zero!
Q4 and full-year FY26 results are out - our first year as a public company. Grateful to 20,000+ team members across 30+ nationalities who made this possible.

Q4:
• Revenue: +41%
• EBITDA: nearly doubled
• PAT (adj): 2.6x last year
• India same-store sales growth: 24%

FY26:

• 23.8 million eye tests (+48.5%) - half of them first-time

But this is not the peak.

We are serving 50 million people in a world where billions need better vision. The problem is big and getting bigger - and as we go deeper, the opportunity widens. Smart glasses have opened an entirely new dimension over and above.

And AI has given us wings we have been waiting for.

Every eye test, every transaction, every frame tried on - it all generates data. That data now compounds on itself. Lenskart is no longer just an eyewear company. We are an eyewear + data company.

We're building for the next billion. The best is yet to come.

Q1 FY27 Key Numbers:

EBITDA: ₹589 Cr | 21.7% margin
PAT: ₹228 Cr | +182% YoY

Q1 PAT of ₹228 Cr - compared with ₹530 Cr for the whole of FY26.

The big story this quarter is International. Revenue grew 38%, with EBITDA (pre-IndAS 116) margin crossing 10%. Owndays continues to strengthen in Japan, while Meller’s Paris store is seeing queues daily, with London next. Meller is tracking towards a ~$70M global brand.

And the engine in India keeps getting stronger:
• 0.7 Cr eye tests, up 39.8%
• Roughly 35,000 Indians discover every day at Lenskart that they need vision correction
• 18.3% India SSSG
• 70%+ product margin for the first time
• 80,000+ sign-ups for B by Lenskart, with smart glasses now shipping everyday
• Self-eye testing has entered pilot stores

The last one year has made one thing very clear to me:

We have to build the infrastructure for vision care. You cannot train your way to a billion eye tests. You have to engineer your way there.

AI + eye care + data + smart glasses gives us the opportunity to fundamentally expand access to vision.

Grateful to every customer, every Lenskartian and our shareholders.

Still very early. Still lots to learn.
Still Day Zero. 🙏

Today is American Business Women’s Day, and I keep thinking about how recently women could be required to have a man’s signature to get a business loan.

Some states still required women to have a husband or other male relative co-sign a business loan until 1988?! What?! That was only 12 years before I started @spanx.

The progress came in steps. In 1974, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act made it illegal to deny women credit or require a male co-signer simply because they were women. Then, in 1988, the Women’s Business Ownership Act eliminated state laws requiring a husband or other male relative to co-sign a woman’s business loan - and expanded support for women entrepreneurs.

Not that long ago, a woman’s ability to access credit could depend on a man’s signature instead of her own ambition and ability to build. 🤯

Think of all the businesses, ideas, and inventions that may not have had the chance to exist before then.

I’m a big believer that the more women-owned businesses we have in this world, the better. ❤️

Tag a woman whose business you’re so glad exists. ⬇️ 

#AmericanBusinessWomensDay #WomenOwnedBusiness #FemaleEntrepreneur

Nothing will matter more than your opinion of yourself. Do things that make you proud, be kind, crack yourself up, help others, try new things, manage negative self talk, give yourself a break, become self aware, become a student of yourself, you are fascinating (believe me we all are), spend time alone, take yourself on vacation. If you are chasing approval from others just know their approval often has nothing to do with you (same with their dislike). It’s something you can’t control. It’s affected by the baggage they’re carrying, or the lens they’ve created through their own unique experiences. When you realize what others think of you has almost nothing to do with you, it will free you up to focus on the thing that really matters… do you like you? That’s where you should spend your energy. 😘

linkedin.about:
Hey, I am Sharan Hegde, better known as Finance With Sharan.

With 1 Crore+ followers across Instagram, YouTube & LinkedIn and X, you have probably seen my finance videos pop up in your feed. But LinkedIn is where I tell a different story. This is where I build in public.

Right now, with a team of 200+ people, I am building something I genuinely believe Indians have been waiting for: an AI-first personal finance app inside 1% Club.

But before I get there, a little backstory.

It started in school, when I could not crack IIT (the classic Indian household story). That setback made me fiercely competitive. In 2019, I chased a promotion as a management consultant. Two years of grind got me a 5% raise and no promotion. Setback two. Then I attempted CAT 2021 dreaming of IIM Bangalore. Setback three.
I am sure this resonates with a lot of you.

So I treated every failure as feedback, and Finance With Sharan was born. The mission was simple: make finance simple, fun, and actually useful.

2 years ago I started the 1% Club to help people become financially independent. Today we are SEBI-licensed (RIA & RA), backed by Gruhas, and profitable. 

My simple problem statement behind all this is that:

Most of us juggle a broker, a bank, three card apps, an insurance portal. Each does one thing okay. None of them helps you think across your full money picture.

That is what we are fixing. An AI co-pilot that sees your complete financial life, answers in plain language, and nudges you before you make a mistake. Not generic internet advice, or an expensive human advisor you do not trust. Something in between, built for the Indian middle that has real money decisions but no one to ask.

Financial independence is a superpower. Less than 1% of people get there in their lifetime.

We are building the thing that gets you there.

posts.text:
I met an NRI in the US who pays $10,000 every month just to live in New York City.

I sat down with Khushi Jain, a 25-year-old from Gurgaon and a well-known Instagram creator, for The 1% Club Show in her New York apartment.

She came to the US at 18 to swim competitively and study. By freshman year, everything changed. She dropped swimming, dropped her pre-med plans, and picked up psychology and marketing instead.

Today she's married, has close to 500,000 followers, and runs her own startup in New York.
But one number from our conversation stuck with me.

She spends $10,000 every month just to live a comfortable life in New York. That's close to ₹10 lakh, every single month.

~ Rent alone in Manhattan starts at $10,000. Move to Brooklyn or Queens, and it drops to $5,000-6,000.

~ Her first job paid her $100,000 a year at 22. In New York, she still felt like she was living hand-to-mouth.

~ Taxes take away another 30-35% of that income, going up to 45% if you're a high earner.

Here's the part that actually surprised me. If you're on a work visa like H-1B, you can't legally earn from content or run a business on the side.

Khushi could only start her own company after she moved to a spouse visa with a work permit.

Her startup, Preserve, connects creators to people who need content, on demand. She even grew 100,000 followers just by filming her own wedding.

Moving abroad looks glamorous from the outside. The real cost, and the real rules, almost never make it to Instagram.

Full episode link in comments.

Vijay Deverakonda is entering the crowded skincare market with Unhype, targeting young Indian consumers through a celebrity-led brand.

You've probably bought a "celebrity" brand the celebrity never used once.  A year ago, Vijay met the Unhype team and was asked to do something most celebrity deals don't: get involved in building the product, not just promoting it.

With Unhype, he took a much more hands-on approach. He was involved in the formulation and testing, not just the launch event.  

What stands out about Unhype is that the creator’s role goes beyond promotion. He is involved in formulation and testing, putting his own involvement behind the product, not just the endorsement. 

The product went through 9 months of testing before it reached the market, including testing on his own skin.

That level of involvement is what caught my attention, because it is similar to how I think about building The 1% Club. 

I didn't build The 1% Club just to talk about money on the internet. I built it by doing the boring work myself first, learning what actually works, and then building something people could trust.  

So the question I keep coming back to is this: how many of the celebrity brands you've bought from were actually built by the person whose face is on them, and how many were just a name that got rented out for a season?

3 years ago, I sat across from Robert Kiyosaki for a podcast. He's now $1.2 billion in debt, on purpose.

He's the man who wrote Rich Dad Poor Dad, a book that shaped how an entire generation, including me, first learned to think about money.

Recently, he's been going on podcasts saying something that sounds alarming at first. He says he's $1.2 billion in debt, and he doesn't seem worried about it at all.

There’s an important detail behind that $1.2 billion number: it isn't all personal debt.  part that actually matters. According to Kim Kiyosaki, his former wife and business partner, it represents debt held across a group of partner-owned real-estate investments, reportedly including roughly 1,500 apartment units. 

The idea behind it is fairly simple once you break it down. When a property he owns rises in value, he refinances instead of selling and paying tax on the profit. The logic is to repeat the cycle over time: buy an asset, earn rental income, let the property appreciate, refinance, and 
reinvest.

He also doesn't hold everything under one company. He splits his properties across many smaller ones, which he calls firewalls, so that if one investment goes wrong, it doesn't drag down the rest.

But this only works while property prices keep rising and tenants keep paying rent. If prices fall sharply, that same debt becomes very hard to service, and separate companies won't fully protect you from a downturn that hits everything at once.

Kiyosaki himself says not to copy this strategy blindly. Leverage can build wealth quickly, but if you don’t understand the debt, the same strategy can work against you just as quickly.

Have you ever used a property's rising value to reinvest instead of cashing out?

When Shah Rukh Khan invests in a tech company, we need to dive deeper. 

Flam builds content that you can actually control. This week they raised 40 million dollars in their latest funding round. It was led by QED Investors, and other backers like Claypond Capital, Martin Chavez, Olivier Pomel, Venky Harinarayan and Shah Rukh Khan joined in. Their older investors, RTP Global and Dovetail, put in even more money too.

What caught my eye was not the money. It was who is already using this. Flam works with more than 100 big companies, and names like Google, Reliance and Hyundai are already on that list.

Here is what they actually do, in the simplest way I can explain it.

1> Flicks, an interactive video where the person or product on screen can change while it is still playing

2> Airboards, 3D content you can touch and talk to, and it loads in less than a second with no app needed

3> Visual Agents, AI characters you can talk to like a video call, and they reply to you in under a second!

Shourya Agarwal, the founder of Flam, said something simple that stayed with me. He said content has always moved one way, from the person who makes it to the person who watches it, and he believes that is about to change.

I think he is right, and here is why it matters to someone like me.

This former IMF economist explained to me why an average Indian earns 5 times less than an average Chinese person.

I sat down with Sriram Balasubramanian, a former IMF economist, for The 1% Club Show.

China's income per person today is around $13,000-14,000. India's is close to $2,500-3,000. 
But here's the twist. India was the richest nation on earth for 1600 straight years before we fell behind.

So what actually went wrong?

He broke it down in the simplest way:
~ India was never one country back then. It was hundreds of small kingdoms, always busy fighting each other.

~ We had riches, temples, and armies. What we didn't have was unity, so outsiders walked in easily.

~ Even our temples worked like banks. They funded traders who built businesses all across Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia.

So it was never about a lack of money or smartness. It was a lack of togetherness.

His "starter pack" for any country trying to get rich: open up to trade, keep governance stable, stay young and hungry, and always plan 20 years ahead.

India is quietly doing a lot of this right now, which is why he's genuinely optimistic about the next two decades.

We were once the richest place on earth. Nothing says we can't get there again, just with our own playbook this time.

Do you think we can close this income gap in our lifetime?

Adani’s 8 airports earned ₹6,401 crore in non-aeronautical revenue in FY26, including duty-free, food, retail, and parking.

The next time you reach an Indian airport early, look around before you reach the gate. You may end up spending money on things you never planned to buy.

Airports are putting more space and money into food, coffee, shopping, lounges, wellness, and other services because passengers are spending more time inside terminals.

A recent Financial Express report looked at how airport retail in India is changing, and the shift is quite simple to understand.

There are a few reasons behind this change.

→ Airports are sitting on empty spending potential: CAPA India found that 60–70% of domestic passengers and 80–90% of international passengers at major Indian airports did not purchase food, beverages, duty-free products, or retail items 

→ Food has become a bigger part of the experience: Premium restaurants, specialty coffee, and quick-service outlets are becoming important categories inside Indian airports.

→ Airports need more sources of income: Apart from money related to flights, airports also earn from retail, food and drinks, lounges, parking, advertising, hospitality and commercial spaces.

→ Passengers expect more: Travellers are increasingly looking for better food choices, comfortable lounges, digital services, local products and places where they can relax while waiting for their flight.

Modern terminal design intentionally guides you past luxury displays and cafes just to reach your gate, turning waiting time into impulse spending on ₹400 coffees or unplanned purchases.

Airports have perfected the art of monetizing your idle time. Are you spending at the terminal out of genuine need, or simply because the floor plan was engineered to make you buy?

Virat Kohli’s reported ₹21 crore IPL fee shows the earning power of celebrity, but ownership changes how that money compounds. 

Virat’s commercial interests include One8 Commune, WROGN and Agilitas Sports, alongside investments in companies such as Go Digit, Rage Coffee and Blue Tribe Foods.

Some of these are businesses he is associated with, while others are investments where his involvement is financial rather than operational.

Anushka Sharma has built a similar mix through her career. She co-founded Clean Slate Filmz with Karnesh Sharma, launched Nush, and has been linked to investments in businesses including Slurrp Farm and Blue Tribe. She stepped away from Clean Slate Filmz’s operational role in 2022.

Here's the layer under all of this. A fee pays you for your time, it stops the moment you stop showing up. Ownership pays you for risk, so it keeps moving, up or down, long after you've walked away.

Virat's IPL cheque and his stake in Go Digit both get counted as "income." Only one of them can make money while he's asleep.

posts.text:
Some chapters are defined by what you achieve. Others by what you learn along the way.

FY25–26 was a year of both for us.

We took a hard look at our business, went back to the fundamentals, made some difficult choices and stayed focused on building a stronger Honasa for the long term.

Today, we are seeing the impact of that work.

₹2,478.5 Cr in like-for-like revenue
₹230+ Cr EBITDA
₹200+ Cr Profit After Tax
₹100 Cr in Dividend 

But behind these numbers are thousands of people who showed up every day, teams that kept pushing forward, partners who continued to believe in us, and millions of consumers who gave our brands a place in their lives.That is what makes this journey meaningful for us.

As we enter the next decade of Honasa, our ambition remains the same — to build brands that people trust, products that genuinely make a difference, and a company that creates lasting value for all those who are part of the journey.

We have come a long way and we know the most exciting part is still ahead.

Our latest Shareholder Letter captures where we are today, what we have learnt, and what we are building for tomorrow.

Read it here: https://lnkd.in/dB6Kjkcg

The idea that reshaped one of our biggest campaigns came to me on a delayed flight,
somewhere over nothing in particular, with no wifi and nothing to do but stare out of a window for two hours longer than planned. 

I used to resent time like that. An empty afternoon, a slow Sunday, a meeting that got cancelled and left an unplanned gap in the day, I filled all of it as fast as I could, usually with my phone because an empty hour felt like a wasted one.

It took me a while to notice the pattern: almost none of my best thinking happened in the full,
busy hours. Nearly all of it happened in the ones I used to consider dead time. I think we've quietly engineered boredom out of our lives, one notification at a time, without realising it was doing something for us. The mind needs a bit of nothing to actually wander, connect things that don't obviously belong together, and arrive somewhere new.

Now I protect a little bit of that time on purpose. It rarely feels productive while it's happening. It
almost always turns out to have been exactly that.

My health score went from 85 to 95 this year. Top 10% for my age apparently.This score was 70 a couple of years back. But honestly the number isn't why I'm writing this. 

What actually changed things for me was realizing pretty late, that a woman's body isn't the same as a male body. Our hormones, our cycles, our nutritional needs at different life stages; none of it works the way most generic health advice assumes. They are crafted for a male body. 

I spent years following workout regimes and taking supplements that were never really built keeping a woman's body in mind and wondering why they weren't doing much for me.

That's a big part of why we decided to start Honasa Health. We want women in India to actually understand their own bodies instead of following a playbook written for someone else. The gap is real it shows up in your blood work, in your health score, in ways you can literally see on paper.

So if you're someone who takes care of everyone else first — ask yourself if you actually know what your own body needs or if you are just guessing.

You can't keep showing up for everyone else if you're running on empty. I'll continue sharing more from my own journey and busting some of the ill-advised myths I see so many women following, often wondering why their regimes aren't getting them anywhere close to their health goals.

The way we discover brands is changing and AI is becoming a big part of that change.

For years, consumers have searched, scrolled, compared and reviewed before making a purchase. Today, more of those questions are moving into conversations with AI. From “What should I use for my skin?” to “Which product is right for me?”, discovery is becoming more personal, contextual and conversational.

At Honasa Consumer Ltd., we’ve always believed that building brands starts with understanding where the consumer is going, not just where they are today. That’s why we’re excited to be the 1st Indian company to advertise on ChatGPT, in partnership with Criteo bringing Mamaearth into this new era of consumer discovery.

For me, this is less about a new advertising platform and more about recognising a new consumer behaviour as it takes shape.

AI is changing the interface between consumers and brands. Our partnership with Criteo is an opportunity to be early to this shift to learn, experiment and explore how technology can make brand discovery more relevant and genuinely useful for consumers.

The future of consumer discovery is already taking shape. At Honasa, we’re excited to be right there with it.

One thing I’ve learnt as a founder:
your job changes as your company grows

In the early days, you’re doing everything yourself. You’re solving problems, making decisions, chasing things down and figuring it out as you go.

But as you scale, the real challenge becomes knowing where you should spend your time.

Because not every problem needs a founder.

I’ve increasingly realised that the more we can take complexity out of the way whether through better processes, better teams or better technology the more time we create for the things only a founder can do.

-Think bigger.
-Understand your consumer better.
-Build what doesn’t exist yet.
-And keep asking, “What can we do better?”

That’s where tools like Emergent Ai have been interesting for us. By simplifying operational workflows they can take some of the busywork off the table and create more room for the work that actually moves the business forward.

If you’re a young founder, here’s something I wish more people told me early on:

You don’t have to have it all figured out.

-Start with a real problem
-Stay close to your consumer
-Build consistently
-Don’t be afraid to use every tool available to you to move faster.

You will learn more by building than you ever will by waiting to be ready.

And if you’re already building keep going.The messy middle is where most of the learning happens.

Here’s to the next generation of founders building with ambition, curiosity and a willingness to keep figuring it out.

Presenting Little Steps School by Honasa Consumer Ltd., an initiative to provide education to underprivileged kids between two and six years of age.
 
Varun Alagh and I dreamt of this two years back, and our team has helped us bring it to life so beautifully. This has also been possible because of our partners I.S.R.N (Indian Social Responsibility Network)
 — thank you for believing in this with us.
 
We celebrated Independence Day at Honasa's Little Steps, hoisting the tricolour with the kids, talking to their parents, laughing with them and simply being present in the moment.
 
It took me back to a belief that has been at the heart of Honasa since we started building this House of Brands: the children of India deserve better.
 
Ten years on, that belief continues to guide us.
 
Through Little Steps, we have two centres in Gurugram, supporting 60 children from underserved communities. In addition to this, our bigger centre with 120 kids is coming soon. We focus on the things that can shape a child's life early on: foundational education, nutrition, healthcare, play, and a safe environment to grow.
 
India's future is not some distant idea. It is sitting in these classrooms today and giving these children a stronger foundation is one way we can help make that future a little more equal.
 
I am proud that a belief we started with a decade ago continues to find its way into the work we do today. That, to me, is what building a company with purpose looks like.

If you’re planning to bring something new to the market, then this is for you. I’ve learnt it the hard way.

Most founders don’t fail because they have too few ideas. They struggle because they have too many things happening at once.

When you’re building a new product, category or business, there’s always a long list of things that need fixing.

Awareness. Trust. Distribution. Pricing. Retention. Content. The list keeps growing.

And as a founder, it’s tempting to attack all of them at once. You bring in more people, create more plans, add more initiatives and keep pushing for momentum.

But sometimes, all you’ve created is activity.

The question I’ve learnt to ask is much simpler:

What is the one obstacle that, if we solve it, makes everything else easier?

Once you find that, the job is to make one clear bet around it.

Not ten strategies. Not a long list of initiatives.

Just one strong hypothesis about what will move the business forward — and then 2–3 actions that reinforce each other.

That’s where I’ve seen the real difference between being busy and actually building momentum.

Because when your product, consumer insight, distribution and communication are all working towards the same outcome, every action starts making the next one more effective.

As founders, we’re often rewarded for how much we can take on.

But as the business grows, I think the bigger skill is knowing what not to take on.

The discipline to choose one problem.

The conviction to make one bet.

And the patience to let the right things compound.

If you’re building something new, don’t start by asking, “What all should we do?”

Start by asking:

“What is the one thing that needs to work?”

That answer might change the entire way you strategise your launch.

“Don’t make decisions out of fear.”

Ask any founder how many times they’ve heard that, and the count will probably tell you something about how uncomfortable we are with fear in decision-making.

I think the problem isn’t fear itself. It’s what we do after we feel it.

Early on, whenever I felt anxious about a decision, I assumed it meant I was about to make the wrong one. Over time, I realised fear was rarely asking me to stop. More often, it was asking me to prepare better.

Part of this comes down to how we naturally respond to risk. Prospect Theory suggests that we experience the pain of a loss more intensely than the pleasure of an equivalent gain. In business, that can make potential losses feel more immediate than potential gains, pushing us to avoid big risks even when the upside is worth considering.

One habit that has helped me is giving fear a specific shape. Instead of sitting with general anxiety, I try to identify what I’m actually worried about. Once I can articulate the risk, it becomes something I can plan for, reduce or account for rather than something that quietly influences my decision.

Fear doesn’t always signal danger. Sometimes it simply reflects that the decision matters.
I’ve found that founders who appear fearless are usually those who acknowledge their fears, understand them and keep moving anyway.

For me, fear has become less of a stop sign and more of a prompt to think carefully before committing.

#Entrepreneurship #Leadership

My mornings don’t change much. Same quiet 30 minutes before anyone needs anything from me. Same handful of decisions I don’t have to think about — what I eat, when I move, when the laptop opens and when it shuts. None of it photographs well. None of it would make an interesting reel on its own.

But here’s what I’ve noticed — the days that go well aren’t the days something exciting happens. They’re the days the boring stuff already happened, so I have the bandwidth left for whatever actually needs my full attention. A predictable routine isn’t the opposite of ambition. It’s what makes ambition sustainable past the first few months of adrenaline. 
  If your day feels chaotic, the fix probably isn’t a better morning routine video. It’s picking a handful of boring decisions and making them non-negotiable, so your energy stops leaking out through a hundred small choices you didn’t need to make in the first place.

Discipline isn’t dramatic. It’s just consistent. And consistent, it turns out, is the closest thing to a cheat code any of us actually get.

When my husband and co-founder, decided to put our savings into building a business almost everyone around us questioned the decision.

 Honestly, they had valid reasons too.

But we believed we had found a problem worth solving.

That’s what entrepreneurship is really about- 
having the conviction to follow an opportunity, while being smart enough to test that conviction with data.

Don’t let someone else’s fear become your limitation.

If you believe there’s a real problem worth solving
listen to yourself, validate it with data, and give yourself a chance to find out.

posts.text:
Is the Regulator asking the right question?

IRDAI's own paper says premiums grew but coverage did not grow enough.
Costs stayed high over time.

After commissions went into one company cost pot, payouts to distributors grew faster than premium.

So there are two problems. 
Costs are high. 
Coverage is thin.

I am not defending fat commissions 😅
Credit life sold with a loan at high commission is a mess.

But is commission the main reason India is at about 3.7% insurance penetration while the world is near 7%? 
That link is not clearly proven.

If you slash selling incentives before you prove price was the barrier, fewer people will sell. 
Then fewer policies. 
The coverage problem gets worse.

Employment in the industry could also get affected for no obvious & immediate benefit 🤷🏻

Its still early. 
Phase the cut. 
Prove the barrier first.

Anyone calling MDR on UPI a tax is smoking something heavy 😅

UPI costs about Rs 20,700 crore a year to run. 
The Budget puts in Rs 2,000 crore of our money. 
Banks and apps eat the rest. 

That is not a free market. That is a subsidised monopoly.

Introducing a low MDR is the right move.
But to keep it that way, we have to ask a deeper question.
Why is there only one NPCI?

In 2020, RBI itself invited rivals.
6 consortiums with serious capital, like TATA & Reliance, applied.
In 2023 the plan was shelved.

Instead we announced a 30% market share cap in 2020.
Still deferred coz 2 apps hold over 85%.

Takeaway👇🏼
You cannot mandate competition. 
You have to enable it.

Telecom had one sarkari operator. 
We opened it up and got some of the cheapest data in the world. 

Visa and Mastercard charge 2% because they are a duopoly. 
Five rails fighting for every merchant cannot.

Enable five NPCIs. 
Kill the subsidy. Let them fight. 
MDR will always stay negligible 🤷🏼‍♂️

India’s biggest startup opportunities often look boring before they look obvious.

UPI did. So did the internet.

At the turn of the century, a marriage broker walked into my father’s office carrying biodatas in a bag.

I remember thinking, how many profiles can one man carry?

The internet was the new rail. Shaadi.com was simply a business built on top of it.

Now another rail is quietly getting built.
Account Aggregator.

Terrible name. Potentially massive opportunity 😅

The RBI-regulated ecosystem has crossed 500 million fulfilled consents, and AA-enabled lending reportedly reached ₹3.82 lakh crore in FY26.

Yet every second pitch I see is still some version of ‘AI for X’.
Nothing wrong with AI.

But we often obsess over the shiny layer and miss the infrastructure changing underneath.

AA could do the same for lending, wealth, insurance, underwriting and financial identity.

The real edge may not always be inventing the future.

Sometimes it is noticing the boring pipe before everyone else sees the water flowing through it 💰

India mein sabko ‘Riddhi’ chahiye ...
Lekin sirf Vidhi se not possible 🤷🏻

Nidhi Tuteja Dua & Rajat Dua walked onto Shark Tank India with Nidhi’s Grandmaa Secret
A 13-herb hair oil made from a family recipe in their Gurugram kitchen. 

They even drank it on camera to prove a point 🤮
Disgusting, but impressive

2 yrs later, they’re shipping pan-India and doing 30 cr ARR. Crazzzyy ..

My takeaway? 
It all starts with showing up 💪🏼

Riddhi chahiye? Be a Nidhi first
Baaki hum dekh lenge 🦈

Got a great business in your kitchen or garage?
Don't leave it to fate. Show up & Scale up.

Season 6 Delhi auditions begin 3rd September👊🏼

Could this be transformational for our country?

Regardless, this kid needs to be applauded for the sheer audacity & can-do attitude that has the potential to improve governance & accountability in our country.

Hopefully, GenZ & Alpha will follow his example and bring meaningful change to India 🇮🇳 Truly inspiring 

P:S - Pls reshare so ppl can add their experiences to bribes.fyi & it becomes too big to fail

India is where pricing strategies come to die!
 
Every few years, a global tech company arrives with $ converted to Rs.
 
Then India happens 😅
 
We share subscriptions. Stretch free trials. Find jugaad workarounds.
 
And finally ask the only question that matters...Bhai, isse mera kya hoga?
 
When we were building Shaadi.com, the lesson came early. Indians pay when the outcome becomes important enough.
 
That distinction is now coming for AI.
 
As AI companies roll out India-specific plans,  I think they are being schooled in value.
 
India is not a cheaper version of America. It is a far more demanding market with customers who can smell ‘chep raha hai’ from a km away 😉
 
If an AI product can become useful, affordable and habit-forming here, It will become a better product everywhere.
 
India did this to telecom, payments and entertainment.
 
Now AI gets its turn. 🤖🇮🇳

This chair isn’t unclaimed ...

It’s waiting for a woman to return.

73% of Indian women leave the workforce,
after marriage or childbirth. 
Two-thirds never return.

We call it a career break.
The truth is, it’s a marriage penalty.

It costs women their freedom and India nearly $350 billion every year.

This Independence Day, Shaadi.org and Aspire For Her,
are helping women reclaim their seats with a community built for their return.

Because independence without financial independence is incomplete.

Ready to return? Register here 👇🏼
https://lnkd.in/daJE9p9f

#HerIndependence 👊🏼
Happy 80th Independence Day 🇮🇳

I am surrounded my women who are rarely the quieter sex.

My mother, sisters, maasis, saalis, my wife, my daughter & the strong women I  work with.

Perhaps that’s why the idea of women needing ‘empowerment’ is a little odd.
They don’t need saving. They need the obstacles removed.

Nearly half our workforce at People Group is female. 

Through Shaadi.com, we support the Udayan Care Shalini Fellowship, which has helped over 18,500 girls from disadvantaged backgrounds complete their education, build careers, and return as mentors to the next generation.

So when L'Oréal Paris and Shark Tank India Tank India opened this season by inviting women founders first, I was stoked 💪🏼

Bcs while women-led startups receive less than 10% of startup finding, on Shark Tank,  ~40% of the cos we've backed have had at least one woman founder.

Not charity. Good investing💰

And based on what I am seeing with Gen Z & Gen Alpha,
We can now dream of a nation where talent matters more than chromosomes🤞🏼

That transition may shape India more profoundly than AI or tech will.
And I’m rooting for it 🙌 🇮🇳

confidence.note: High confidence on career, tone, interests, and values because the signals repeat across both profiles. Lower confidence on private-life fit because the public material is heavily work- and brand-centered, and it also explicitly mentions an existing wife/daughter family context.

reasons.masabagupta: Best overall mutual match: systems-meets-feelings blunt honesty with playful builder chemistry, and the agent feedback (86) says Masaba’s respect for your “no fixing theatre” boundary looks unusually durable—just manage the shared founder high-output intensity.
reasons.mcuban: Very strong long-term founder compatibility with measurable, incentives-driven debate style plus public-ready ease; the only real gap is we didn’t fully stress-test alignment on “work is central” vs “event/roundtable energy,” but rapport and constructiveness were high.
reasons.namitathapar: Deep values alignment (agency, boundaries, blunt equality) and a real recharge-compatible vibe from the hike/date; the main risk is two high-will operators that can turn into subtle power-logic if schedules and recovery aren’t protected.
reasons.leilahormozi: High plan/execute and blunt discipline overlap with a real chance at matching stamina and humor; the main deal-breaker pressure is pure logistics/time-zone reality, plus both being work-central operators.
reasons.peyushbansal: Strong builder overlap on trust, constraints, and Day Zero dignity with chemistry that sounds genuinely easy; main risk is emotional bandwidth/privacy/availability given your very public, family-present life needs consistent private recovery time too.
reasons.aliabdaal: Solid systems/playful chemistry and values overlap with a reflection-friendly pace, but the mismatch risk is your very high-visibility Mumbai founder-investor cadence and the practical long-distance logistics (UK/HK vs your life).
reasons.ryanserhant: While mindset overlap is real (builders + systems + curiosity), the lifestyle cadence (show-first optimism/rituals), geography impracticality, and performative-selling pull make it the weakest for your “infrastructure-precision + sustained work-center” needs.

decision.note: Anupam, I’m picking Masaba Gupta as the top match: your dates indicate the rare combo of mutual respect for your ambition, blunt honesty, and playful builder chemistry without needing a rescue dynamic. Mark Cuban is the closest “runner-up” for long-term founder compatibility and public readiness, while Namita is the strongest values-alignment alternative if you can actively protect recovery and avoid subtle power-logic.

Get out of office, you don’t know how to lead. 
- Ms. Singh

Usually, I am your daddy. But today, I am your father 💫 

Thank you @misho_designs for this custom fit for the @lucasmuseum opening night. 

Styling: @benjaminholtrop / @emilykejohnson 
Hair: @kattthompson 
Make Up: @aaronpaulbeauty 
Fit & Jewellery: @misho_designs

Some men discovered women’s rights this week. Unfortunately, there is required reading.

These views are mine and mine alone. I say them as a fan of this league who is fiercely protective of its players, as someone who has put my own money behind the growth of women’s professional sports, and as someone who has spent a significant part of my career advocating for women and gender equity.

And I’m standing ten toes down against people using women’s safety as a costume for some clout. Sit ALL the way down with your transphobia and tomfoolery. And stop making a mockery of the most successful WNBA season yet.
Sisters, either set boundaries.. or your immune system will. Now if you’ll excuse me, I need to sit under my thyroid red light device 💯✌🏽
Not saying you should passively aggressively send this to anyone… but I’m also not saying you shouldn’t 💅🏽

Why do we reward women for giving everything up? @sanyamalhotra_ and I unpack one of the most deeply ingrained beliefs about womanhood.

We’re taught to admire the woman who sacrifices the most. The mother who always puts herself last. The wife who always compromises. The daughter who never asks for too much. We call it strength. We call it love. We call it being a “good woman.”

But what if we’ve been confusing self-sacrifice with self-worth?

This conversation is about unlearning. About realizing that just because something has always been expected of women doesn’t mean it’s right. Sometimes the bravest thing a woman can do isn’t give more of herself. It’s stop believing she has to.
This one might change the way you see yourself.

Watch the full conversation with Sanya on @YouTube. Link in bio. Also available on @spotify and @apple (link in bio).

For more, follow @shamelesswithlillysingh

analysis.summary: Lilly is a builder with a performer's timing. She runs Unicorn Island, co-founded HYPHEN8, and signed on as part-owner and Chief Hype Officer of the Toronto Tempo, Canada's first WNBA team — all while leading, writing and producing her first feature film. Her own words for what drives it: "I'm on a mission to use storytelling to change the culture around how we treat girls and women." She is funny, blunt and unbothered about being seen doing it: she'll post a two-Anthem-Award team win and a self-deprecating joke about a new outfit in the same week. Underneath the hype energy is someone asking sharper questions than most — about self-sacrifice, boundaries, and why women get rewarded for giving everything up.

York University graduate, NYT best-selling author, UN SDG Advocate, and currently unpacking "one of the most deeply ingrained beliefs about womanhood" in long-form conversation.
She posts yearly impact recaps, thanks publications graciously, and is candid about needing rest and boundaries — though the pace she keeps suggests she's still practising that one.

lifestyle.pace: Furious and multi-threaded — running a production company, a new network, a haircare brand, a gameshow and two sports teams in overlapping windows.
